owner_tempo_followup_english_translation: Regarding MSQ-97: I shoot the enemy, hits make him retreat, and that is fine. I want a sharper, faster response and faster attempts to regain balance by stepping. We will tune this further, but for now it seems it should be about 25 percent faster.
decision: Execute MSQ-92 on MSQ-97 Candidate07 and include an approximately 25 percent faster recovery response and stepping tempo as the initial owner-test tuning.
controller_interpretation: Use a 1.25 recovery-speed baseline, giving comparable phase/reaction durations divided by 1.25 (20 percent shorter), then bounded disturbance-dependent adaptation. Do not accelerate the world, rifle, damage or get-up animation, increase hit impulse, or promise a fixed observed completion time under different physical disturbances.
execution: One existing Multica Unreal executor, verified native Astra/max/standard, focused self-checks, one primary independent technical reviewer. Previous MSQ-91/MSQ-97 review waivers do not extend to MSQ-92.
acceptance: Controller scope, evidence applicability, preservation and finding closure; final motion/play judgement stays with the owner. Preserve predecessor immutable candidates and reuse unaffected evidence.
boundaries: Static flat support, no automatic successor start, new art, general locomotion, expanded counterbalance or new paid services. Controller owns the local task-scoped closure commit.
